seo_title: Audio device priority switcher for macOS
seo_description: OutputRanker is a free, open-source menu bar app that ranks your audio inputs and outputs and automatically switches to the best connected device.
hero_sub: OutputRanker lives in the menu bar and switches your Mac to the highest-ranked connected input and output. Cycle devices anytime with global hotkeys, with a volume HUD.
features_sub: One job done well: decide which device the Mac should use, and switch to it for you.

features.title: Drag to rank devices
features.desc: Outputs and inputs each get their own list that you reorder by dragging in Settings. Disconnected devices stay greyed out in place, so their rank is kept.

features.title: Automatic switching
features.desc: When a device appears or disappears, the highest-ranked connected one becomes the default. If a device fails to take over, the next in the list is tried.

features.title: Manual override when needed
features.desc: Pick a device from the menu and it holds until the device list next changes. Inputs and outputs are overridden separately, and Auto Switch can be turned off entirely.

features.title: Global cycle hotkeys
features.desc: Cycle outputs and inputs from anywhere with Control-Option-Command plus a letter you choose. The defaults are O for outputs and I for inputs.

features.title: On-screen volume HUD
features.desc: After a switch, a click-through panel shows the device name and its volume. Choose its duration from 0.5 to 5 seconds and its position at top, center or bottom.

features.title: Volume remembered per device
features.desc: Each device's volume is saved and restored when you switch back to it. You can also hide devices, such as virtual drivers, from switching and cycling.

permissions_step: No special permissions are required. If you enable Launch at login, macOS may list OutputRanker under System Settings > General > Login Items.

faq.q: Is OutputRanker really free and open source?
faq.a: Yes. It is released under the MIT license and the full source is on GitHub. There is no account, no server and no analytics, and optional donations on Ko-fi are the only way to support it.

None. Hotkeys use Carbon, so Accessibility is not needed, and the HUD is just a window the app draws, so Screen Recording is not needed. It never captures audio, so it does not ask for Microphone access either.
Only on your Mac, in UserDefaults. That includes your device rankings (as device IDs), hidden devices, device names and per-device volumes. Nothing is sent anywhere.
Notarization requires a paid Apple Developer account, and this is a free project. Right-click the app and choose Open once to run it, or build it yourself from source with Xcode and XcodeGen.
